title: Rigveda 10.132: To Mitra and Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.132: To Mitra and Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.132 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Mitra and Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 121r-122r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.132.1-2 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 20); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 121r
translation.original_text:
1ī̱jā̱nam id dyaur gū̱rtāva̍sur ījā̱nam bhūmi̍r a̱bhi pra̍bhū̱ṣaṇi̍ | ī̱jā̱naṁ de̱vāv a̱śvinā̍v a̱bhi su̱mnair a̍vardhatām ||
2tā vā̍m mitrāvaruṇā dhāra̱yatkṣi̍tī suṣu̱mneṣi̍ta̱tvatā̍ yajāmasi | yu̱voḥ krā̱ṇāya̍ sa̱khyair a̱bhi ṣyā̍ma ra̱kṣasa̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1MAY Dyaus the Lord of lauded wealth, and Earth stand by the man who offers sacrifice, And may the Aṣvins, both the Gods, strengthen the worshipper with bliss.
2As such we honour you, Mitra and Varuṇa, with hasty zeal, most blest, you who sustain the folk. So may we, through your friendship for the worshipper, subdue the fiends.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 121r (OPenn image 120, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.131.5 ‹abhiṣṇak›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 121v, begins in RV 10.132.3 ‹abhi priyaṁ rekṇaḥ patyamānāḥ›. Verses 10.132.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.132.3-6 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 20); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 121v
translation.original_text:
3adhā̍ ci̱n nu yad didhi̍ṣāmahe vām a̱bhi pri̱yaṁ rekṇa̱ḥ patya̍mānāḥ | da̱dvām̐ vā̱ yat puṣya̍ti̱ rekṇa̱ḥ sam v ā̍ra̱n naki̍r asya ma̱ghāni̍ ||
4a̱sāv a̱nyo a̍sura sūyata̱ dyaus tvaṁ viśve̍ṣāṁ varuṇāsi̱ rājā̍ | mū̱rdhā ratha̍sya cāka̱n naitāva̱taina̍sāntaka̱dhruk ||
5a̱smin sv e̱3̱̍tac chaka̍pūta̱ eno̍ hi̱te mi̱tre niga̍tān hanti vī̱rān | a̱vor vā̱ yad dhāt ta̱nūṣv ava̍ḥ pri̱yāsu̍ ya̱jñiyā̱sv arvā̍ ||
6yu̱vor hi mā̱tādi̍tir vicetasā̱ dyaur na bhūmi̱ḥ paya̍sā pupū̱tani̍ | ava̍ pri̱yā di̍diṣṭana̱ sūro̍ ninikta ra̱śmibhi̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
3And when we seek to win your love and friendship, we.who have precious wealth in our possession, Or when the worshipper augments his riches let not his treasures be shut up
4That other, Asura! too was born of Heaven. thou art, O Varuṇa, the King of all men. The chariot's Lord was well content, forbearing to anger Death by sin so great.
5This sin hath Ṣakapûta here committed. Heroes who fled to their dear friend he slayeth, When the Steed bringeth down your grace and favour in bodies dear and worshipful.
6Your Mother Aditi, ye wise, was purified with water even as earth is purified from heaven. Show love and kindness here below: wash her in rays of heavenly light.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 121v (OPenn image 121, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.132.3 ‹abhi priyaṁ rekṇaḥ patyamānāḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 122r, begins in RV 10.132.7 ‹tā naḥ kaṇūkayantīr nṛmedhas›. Verses 10.132.3-6 end on this page; 10.132.3 begins on fol. 121r.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.132.7 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 7, varga 20); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 122r
translation.original_text: <sup>7</sup>yu̱vaṁ hy a̍pna̱rājā̱v asī̍data̱ṁ tiṣṭha̱d ratha̱ṁ na dhū̱rṣada̍ṁ vana̱rṣada̍m | tā na̍ḥ kaṇūka̱yantī̍r nṛ̱medha̍s tatre̱ aṁha̍saḥ su̱medha̍s tatre̱ aṁha̍saḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>7</sup>Ye Twain have seated you as Lords of Wealth, as one who mounts a car to him who sits upon the pole, upon the wood. These our disheartened tribes Nr̥imedhas saved from woe, Sumedhas saved from Woe.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 122r (OPenn image 121, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.132.7 ‹tā naḥ kaṇūkayantīr nṛmedhas›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 122v, begins in RV 10.133.4 ‹adhaspadaṁ tam īṁ kṛdhi›. Verse 10.132.7 ends on this page; 10.132.7 begins on fol. 121v.
